confidence: Kumon's observed rice in nominal monme, 1706-1711, in the Hoei silver (50%, 1.875 g a monme). The ryo and mon rates are one Osaka money-changer's, compiled a century later (Kusama, 1815), and name no city. The wage is borrowed.

monme.note: Hoei silver (1706-1711), 1.875 g pure; Kusama's market rates in Hoei silver, late 1706-1710 (about 62-83 monme a ryo, 40-66 mon a monme), the mean of the rows' midpoints

bu.note: A quarter of a ryo (the gold count: 4 bu a ryo)

shu.note: A sixteenth of a ryo (16 shu a ryo)

rice.label: historical
rice.note: 0.473 monme a kg, Kumon's observed 1706-1711 (6 years)

wage.note: BORROWED: none found for these years; the reference day (0.907 monme) chained by Kumon's farm-servant year, 105.9 monme in 1706-1711 and 113.9 in 1745-1754, in grams of silver
